case_title: Ram Prakash Chadha v. State of Uttar Pradesh
accused_victim_relationship: Employer; the victim was the appellant's cashier/accountant (clerk) for about 13 years
evidence_type: Documentary: final report/chargesheet and Section 161 witness statements; post mortem report referred to
trial_court_outcome: Discharge application under s.227 Cr.PC rejected; charges to proceed against appellant (order dated 19.04.2007)
neutral_facts: The victim was a long-serving cash collector and clerk employed by the accused, who ran a wood business. On 15 July 1993 the victim and a companion were collecting business proceeds from shops. While the victim was inside a shop, two men snatched a bag holding the collection from the companion at gunpoint and fled on a motorcycle. The accused reported this as a robbery to the police. The initial investigation found the report to be false, but the case was later reassigned to another officer. On 17 July 1993 the accused had the victim brought from his home through an employee to the police station for inquiry. According to the later investigation report, the victim was then held at the police station until 23 July 1993 and was tortured during interrogation about the robbery. Late on 23 July he was taken to a hospital by police personnel and was admitted under an unknown name. He died in the early hours of 24 July 1993. A complaint by the accused alleged that police personnel had beaten the victim to death. The post mortem report recorded ante mortem cut incisions on both buttocks. The cause of death could not be ascertained and poisoning was ruled out. Section 161 statements of the victim's widow, son and brother were recorded. Under the investigation report, no police station entry of the custody was made.
physical_harm: Death of the victim in hospital on 24.07.1993 after custody; post mortem showed ante mortem cut incisions on both buttocks, cause of death not ascertained
financial_property_loss: Cash and a draft taken in the robbery case (Crime No.351/1993), belonging to the appellant; amount not stated
key_evidence_accepted: Final report dated 21.02.2000 and Section 161 witness statements, which the Court found contained no accusation against the appellant
witness_credibility: Not assessed for credibility; the Court found no witness statement implicated the appellant in conspiracy or common intention
trial_duration: offence: 17.07.1993 to 23.07.1993 (custody period); trial judgment: order dated 19.04.2007 (discharge rejected); High Court: 21.04.2023; Supreme Court: 15 July 2024
legal_representation: Appellant: Siddhartha Dave, Sr. Adv. (with others). State: Ardhendumauli Kumar Prasad, A.A.G. (with others)
investigation_status: FIR registered; chargesheet (final report) filed 21.02.2000 by CBCID; discharge application pending at trial
procedural_irregularity: High Court did not consider the matter in the manner required under law; the trial court's suspicions were based on suppositions
appeal_history: Trial court: discharge rejected (19.04.2007). High Court: s.482 application dismissed (21.04.2023). Supreme Court: appeal allowed, orders set aside, appellant discharged
prosecution_argument: Appellant lodged the robbery complaint, produced the deceased at the police station, and then lodged the custodial death complaint, creating strong suspicion; concurrent findings should not be interfered with
defence_argument: No material to implicate the appellant under s.120B or s.34 IPC; witness statements carry no accusation of conspiracy; trial court's suspicion was made only by the court
legal_principle_applied: Discharge under s.227 Cr.PC must rest on the record of the case and documents submitted therewith, not suppositions or suspicions; court must disclose reasons for rejection; criminal conspiracy requires an agreement
precedent_relied_upon: State of Orissa v. Debendra Nath Padhi (2005) 1 SCC 568; P. Vijayan v. State of Kerala (2010) 2 SCC 398; Union of India v. Prafulla Kumar Samal (1979) 3 SCC 4; also Yogesh alias Sachin Jagadish Joshi (AIR 2008 SC 2991), State of Tamil Nadu v. N Suresh Rajan ((2014) 11 SCC 709), Om Parkash Sharma v. CBI ((2000) 5 SCC 679), R. Venkatakrishnan v. CBI ((2009) 11 SCC 737), Ajay Aggarwal v. Union of India ((1993) 3 SCC 609)
